firstMismatch.jsEntry: js/wield.js:dowield refuses the quivered weapon before processing the source prompt and split

summary: wield.c:dowield handles the currently quivered stack directly. When the stack can be split and inventory capacity permits, it asks whether to wield one; y splits one object and continues normal wield setup, while q returns. Other answers ask whether to wield the entire stack, clearing uquiver only when accepted. The JS implementation now follows this branch and preserves the remainder in the quiver when one object is wielded. The full admitted replay matches all recorded screens, RNG calls, and cursors.

source.branch: The selected object is uquiver. For a splittable stack with quan>1 and inventory count below invlet_basic, the function asks “Wield one?”; q returns ECMD_OK, y splits one object, calls finish_splitting, then proceeds through ordinary weapon setup. Other answers ask whether to wield all; refusal reports that the stack remains readied, while acceptance clears uquiver. The fallback whole-object prompt uses source singular/plural wording and likewise preserves the quiver on refusal.
callers: wield.c:dowield selects the current uquiver object, calls splitobj/finish_splitting for the one-object choice, and continues through wield setup.

evidence: C source wield.c:dowield (354-457) handles the quiver selection before the ordinary worn-item checks. With a stack and capacity, it prompts whether to wield one, returns for q, and on y uses splitobj(uquiver, 1L), finish_splitting, then continues wield setup.
